notes.summary: RunEngine, CombatEngine, RoomGenerator, and ProgressionStore own all gameplay rules in pure RefCounted scripts over dictionaries so the same codepath powers both the playable scenes and headless regression tests.
UI copy should stay terse and action-oriented; prefer visual communication, concise labels, and lightweight overlays over explanatory panel text or multi-sentence instructions.

RunScene builds the camp-menu and pile-inspector overlays in code; resume vs. new-run flow is chosen from the root meta key 'labyrinth_resume_saved_run' and backed by ProgressionStore's separate saved-run slot.

RunScene sizes MiniMapOverlay in _layout_mini_map_overlay() from the current viewport instead of fixed offsets because a larger static corner map was overflowing smaller windows and obscuring the board.

Combat hands are only dead when both the printed card previews and the drag fallback previews are invalid; Pass logic and hand dimming need to account for the alternate 2-attack and 2-move plays, not just the printed card text.

UI regressions need screenshot probes for combat, pile inspectors, the drag overlay, fallback targeting, and after-play states because those overlays are built in code and scene-instantiation tests miss layout and input breakage.

Multi-action cards treat targeted steps as skippable by default unless an action is marked required; the preview auto-skips dead target steps and the combat choice bar exposes Skip for optional follow-ups that still have valid targets.

Enemy block is preview-time: assigning a revealed intent preloads any block onto the enemy for the current player turn, then enemy phase clears that preview block before actions resolve so it does not carry into the next turn.

Regression tests now lock the updated combat rules: revealed enemy block must mitigate the current player turn immediately, and multi-action cards must stay playable when optional targeted steps can be skipped or auto-skipped.

Targetless cards must commit on the initial click path itself; previewing their resolved state without immediately awaiting _play_player_card leaves a ghost preview that cancels on the next selection instead of spending the card.
Hand-card damage text should come from CombatEngine final-damage and modifier helpers, using a preview-state copy so Ember Lens stays aligned with live combat on multi-action cards.
Pile widgets need collapsed legacy children and short empty captions
notes.details: The dynamic draw/discard/burn widgets still sit on top of the original scene controls, so _build_pile_widget should zero out those legacy children. Empty-pile captions also need to stay short (DECK/DISC/BURN); letting discard render DISCARD can overflow and look like a stretched pile even when the frame is fine.

notes.summary: Hover-lifted cards need unclipped transparent hand scroll
notes.details: The hand ScrollContainer should use an empty panel style and clip_contents=false. Otherwise hovered cards get their tops cut off and the hand row can show a darker panel strip that reads like a mismatched background behind the cards.

notes.summary: Stable card drag needs a top-level proxy and hidden source card
notes.details: The dragged card proxy should be top_level and the source hand widget should be hidden instead of rebuilding the whole hand at drag start. Rebuilding under the cursor or leaving the source visible causes jittery drag behavior and visual fighting between the proxy and the hand layout.

notes.summary: Top-level card proxies must not reuse position-based hover lift
notes.details: CardWidget's hover/selection pose adjusts position.y, which is fine inside the hand layout but breaks top_level drag proxies by snapping them toward y=0. For drag proxies, keep absolute position untouched and only apply safe visual properties like scale.

notes.summary: Elemental combat stores burn, freeze, shock, poison, and stoneskin directly on unit dictionaries so cards, room-tuned enemy intents, board badges, and tests all share one status model.

Enemy threat previews follow the hovered enemy's current intent, keep move_toward/move_away directional, and exclude move tiles from attack tiles so blue movement and red threat overlays stay distinct.

Player freeze and shock badges need to merge player_turn_restrictions with the stored status counters, because prepare_next_player_turn consumes those counters before the board renders the locked turn.
Enemy attack steps now enqueue only when the player state actually changes, and shallow elemental rooms tone down enemy status payloads so freeze/shock pressure ramps up later in the run.
Ice and lightning enemy CC now comes only from rarer intents (weight 2 or less) at depth 3+, and those freeze/shock attacks cap their range at 4 so elemental control pressure ramps more gently.

ActionIconLibrary is the shared source of truth for reusable combat keyword icon tokens, paths, and tooltips; card summaries and combat board intents/status badges should consume its token rows instead of hand-building keyword strings.
Use UiTooltipPanel for custom tooltip overlays
notes.details: Cards and custom-drawn combat board regions should route keyword and modifier tooltip text through UiTooltipPanel so tooltip styling stays consistent and avoids the default translucent black engine tooltip.

notes.summary: Depth-sort board bodies and fade foreground blockers
notes.details: CombatBoardView draws floor/overlays first, then interleaves terrain props and unit bodies in tile draw order. Unit HUDs stay in a final pass for readability. Tall blockers (wall/pillar) tint translucent only when their prop rect overlaps a unit on a farther-back tile, using the same tile comparator as rendering.

notes.summary: The reaver idle sheet should be read in standard row-major order (left-to-right, then top-to-bottom); reordering it column-major makes the idle loop visibly less smooth.

Enemy intent popups reserve a title line for the intent name, including name-only intents like Wait, so layout code and tests should size popups from total intent lines instead of raw action-row count.
Enemy art_scale is applied after fitting, anchored at the fitted rect bottom-center so smaller sprites stay centered horizontally, keep their feet planted, and keep HUD placement stable.
Enemy intent popups now auto-expand to fit their title and token rows, preserving a fixed minimum width while preventing long names like Skitter Strike from clipping.
Move and attack targeting now rely on tile highlights and path lines only; CombatBoardView no longer draws extra preview glyphs like circles or plus signs over target tiles.
Auto room dialogue is keyed by room coord plus turns_spent so _refresh_ui() can safely rerun without reopening the overlay, while revisiting the same room later still retriggers the conversation.

RunEngine traversal now uses square Chebyshev rings with 8*d rooms per depth, cardinal-only perimeter links, 1/4 of each ring linking outward, inward moves locked after advancing, and empty treasure rooms falling back to room mode.
Combat board unit art now honors per-definition art_offset_x/y after fit/scale; adjust sprite centering in enemy/npc data instead of changing global anchoring.
notes.details: Introduced for the Ash Acolyte PNG alignment and covered by _test_enemy_art_offset_shifts_sprite_vertically in tests/run_tests.gd.

notes.summary: CombatBoardView idle animation is fully data-driven per unit: definitions can override idle_sheet_columns, idle_sheet_rows, idle_sheet_order, and idle_frame_seconds while same-stem _idle loading remains automatic.
notes.details: Default behavior stays 4x2 row-major at 0.10s per frame, but Ash Acolyte uses 2x4 column_major at 0.20s per frame; covered by _test_acolyte_idle_sheet_honors_column_major_layout and _test_acolyte_idle_speed_override in tests/run_tests.gd.

notes.summary: Door tiles are blocking terrain for PathUtils, so movement, spawns, threat ranges, and pathfinding all treat room exits like walls.
notes.details: This prevents enemies from spawning or walking onto exit doors and is covered by _test_room_generation_blocks_door_tiles in tests/run_tests.gd.

notes.summary: Enemy HUD collision avoidance moves the full enemy health-plus-intent stack together and draws a tether line when displaced, so overlap fixes still preserve which unit the intent belongs to.
notes.details: CombatBoardView scores small sideways/upward nudges against reserved HUD rects, then falls back to a dynamic escape offset based on the stack bounds for dense overlaps; covered by _test_enemy_hud_layout_stays_centered_when_clear and _test_enemy_hud_layout_offsets_away_from_reserved_ui in tests/run_tests.gd.

notes.summary: NPC combat art basenames can inherit idle sheets by stem, so static placeholder NPCs need a unique art filename with no matching *_idle texture.
notes.details: CombatBoardView auto-loads %s_idle from the art_path basename for both enemies and NPCs. Pointing the Emaciated Man at acolyte.svg pulled in acolyte_idle.png and caused flickering; emaciated_man.svg is intentionally a unique basename with no idle companion.

notes.summary: Multi-action card resolution keeps a target slot per targeted step, using INVALID_TARGET placeholders for skipped steps.
notes.details: RunScene now pads auto-skipped and manually skipped targeted actions with INVALID_TARGET_TILE so animation playback stays aligned with the original action list, which enables one-click move-then-attack enemy shortcuts without misassigning later targets.

notes.summary: Combat board door visibility and move layering are presentation-driven via explicit door and draw-tile maps.
notes.details: run_scene now injects active_door_tiles for connected exits that should still look like doors during combat, locked_door_tiles for sealed traversal doors, and unit_draw_tiles for animated movers so CombatBoardView can keep smooth world-position interpolation without nearest-tile snapping.

notes.summary: Health bar HP text should use a 1px bottom inset instead of the old fixed +10 baseline, or the outlined Press Start 2P digits clip against the top border.
notes.details: The HP readout is drawn inside a 12px bar with a 1px four-direction outline; bottom-anchoring the baseline at rect.size.y - 1 keeps the numerals visually centered and avoids the top-edge clipping that shows up with this pixel font.

notes.summary: Enemy health bars intentionally use a larger 84x14 rect while player bars stay 78x12, because the outlined HP digits still feel cramped in a 12px enemy bar.
notes.details: CombatBoardView bottom-anchors both bars to the same HUD clearance, so enlarging the enemy bar grows it upward into free space without pushing it down into sprite art or breaking intent stacking.

notes.summary: Trap movement paths now minimize trap crossings before distance, and trap-applied freeze/shock/stun on players are deferred through pending_player_trap_restriction so they hit the next possible action after the current card resolves.
notes.details: Voluntary player move previews and move resolution share path_for_player_action, so the previewed route matches the actual step-by-step trap triggers. Enemies treat trap tiles as blocked for intent previews and voluntary movement, but forced movement can still push or pull units through traps and trigger them immediately.

notes.summary: move_to_room must refresh its local rooms snapshot after _reveal_neighbors before non-combat room branches mutate room state, or treasure/campfire/NPC transitions can overwrite newly revealed exits and strand the run in a false dead end.
Crawler intent pacing now leads the roster at 3/2/4 movement with slightly lighter 3/5 melee damage, while acolyte and warden stay at 2 and 1 average movement respectively.
notes.details: tests/run_tests.gd checks crawler/acolyte/warden per-intent movement averages and weighted ordering so the crawler stays the fastest pressure enemy without matching the larger enemies' damage ceiling.

notes.summary: Ash floor variants are extracted as isolated tile-only PNGs and loaded untrimmed so every stone keeps the same isometric canvas and avoids neighbor-fragment warping.
notes.details: The first extraction pass kept surrounding source context inside the diamond, which could make a variant look peeled or skewed in-game. The corrected assets flood-fill the selected tile component from base_floor_tiles.png, keep neighboring tiles transparent, and CombatBoardView now loads the variant textures without trim_texture_to_used_rect.

notes.summary: Card balance work now uses spec/card_balance_heuristic.md and tools/card_heuristic.py as the default curve-check workflow.
notes.details: AGENTS.md tells future sessions to consult the heuristic when creating or modifying cards and to update both the doc and tool whenever combat pacing, status behavior, room spacing, enemy assumptions, fatigue, or action keywords change.

notes.summary: The April 2026 card rebalance preserves standout freeze, shock, poison, and mobility identities by taxing the hottest cards with health costs instead of stripping effects.
notes.details: Weak mobility and melee cards were buffed with cleaner identity-aligned changes: Shadow Step became a pure blink, Venom Claw and Tectonic Maul stayed adjacent melee and gained separate setup/payload, and underperforming air manipulation cards picked up real damage or flow so the heuristic bands close without turning melee attacks into pseudo-ranged cards.

notes.summary: Local card analytics now emit append-only JSONL events through scripts/analytics_store.gd.
notes.details: RunScene owns the instrumentation because it can observe reward picks and before/after combat state. It assigns run/combat ids plus per-combat card instance ids, then logs run/combat/reward events together with card_drawn, card_became_playable, card_played, and enemy_status_tick for offline balancing analysis. spec/analytics.md documents schema version 1; delayed status ticks are currently combat-level rather than card-source attributed.

notes.summary: Boundary wall and door props render with a narrower draw width than their raw fitted texture so each blocker stays inside a single wall tile span.
notes.details: Wall segments still use the tall prop frame and bottom alignment, but _prop_draw_rect now horizontally compresses boundary blockers after fitting: walls use a slightly reduced width and doors use an even narrower inset width so the opening reads as part of one wall segment instead of spilling across neighbors.

notes.summary: Prop-art regression tests should compare trimmed pillar-vs-wall silhouette rather than assuming the pillar stays perfectly square after texture trimming.
notes.details: CombatBoardView trims PNG props to their used rect before fitting. The pillar asset loads with a noticeably squarer silhouette than the wall art, but not a perfect 1:1 ratio, so regression coverage should assert that pillars stay materially broader and squarer than wall segments instead of hard-coding a square threshold.

notes.summary: Room moss now lives in decorative metadata instead of terrain tile IDs.
notes.details: RoomGenerator returns moss.floor/wall/pillar tile lists, CombatEngine/RunEngine carry that metadata through room and combat state, and CombatBoardView renders seeded moss overlay textures on ash floors plus wall/pillar props. This replaces the old moss-terrain approach so passability and floor variants stay purely stone.

notes.summary: With outer wall rendering disabled, CombatBoardView now hides boundary wall tiles by filtering them out of draw and hit-test order while keeping visible doors rendered and clickable.
notes.details: _display_tile_id still resolves hidden boundary doors back to wall semantics, but _tiles_in_draw_order now applies _should_render_tile so only true boundary walls disappear. Active exits and locked presentation doors stay as "door" tiles, which removes the old fake ash perimeter without breaking traversal.

notes.summary: Door presentation uses the supplied isometric door.png directly on ash floor tiles, flipped horizontally for the opposite diagonal.
notes.details: After the user replaced door.png with a transparent tile-oriented asset, CombatBoardView stopped loading generated door_row.png/door_col.png skew variants. Visible doors now draw as a single overlay prop on the regular ash floor tile; row-edge doors use door.png as-is for the bottom-left/top-right diagonal, and col-edge doors use AssetLoader.flip_texture_h for the bottom-right/top-left diagonal.

notes.summary: Door size and placement are hand-tuned through explicit frame scale constants.
notes.details: CombatBoardView uses DOOR_FRAME_WIDTH_SCALE, DOOR_FRAME_HEIGHT_SCALE, and DOOR_BASELINE_OFFSET_SCALE near the top of the file to fit door.png on top of regular ash floor tiles. Increasing width/height scales the rendered door; changing baseline moves the planted floor line without touching the source asset or flip logic.

notes.summary: Door exits show only floating element icons, with rectangular exit label boxes disabled.
notes.details: CombatBoardView no longer calls _draw_exit_marker_for_tile from _draw_scene_objects, so visible door exits keep their icon drawn by _draw_tile_props but no longer render the direction/element label box. The marker function remains in the file if labels need to be restored later.

notes.summary: AOE card actions use explicit pattern offsets: range 0 resolves from the player without a target, while range > 0 targets a visible center tile; rotate=true patterns auto-select the rotation that hits the most relevant units.
notes.details: The card/UI schema stores pattern as JSON offset pairs and optional rotate. CombatEngine validates ranged AOE centers by range/LOS, applies close AOE from the player tile, and exposes aoe_tiles_for_player_action so RunScene previews and animations use the same best-rotation tile set as damage resolution.

notes.summary: Door props use mirrored back-edge offsets with a smaller top-edge scale.
notes.details: CombatBoardView offsets visible door frames toward the outside/back edge, but the top pair are tuned slightly forward with DOOR_TOP_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE while the right and bottom perimeter doors keep DOOR_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE. Keep top-right/top-left mirrored to each other and bottom-right/bottom-left mirrored to each other when retuning door placement.

notes.summary: Room door and minimap icons are centralized in RoomIconLibrary.
notes.details: RunScene sends RoomIconLibrary icon ids to CombatBoardView for room-exit door icons, and LabyrinthMapView uses the same helper for minimap room icons. Keep non-combat destination icons and minimap icons in this helper so door selection and the map stay visually consistent; cleared minimap rooms should be shown by muted grey styling rather than overlaying an X.

notes.summary: Permanent card upgrades stack as generated card mods.
notes.details: Permanent card upgrades now live in progression.card_mods as base_card_id -> Array[mod], with legacy progression.card_upgrades kept only for compatibility. Decks, rewards, analytics ids, and saved runs still keep base card ids; callers resolve behavior through GameData.card_def_for_progression so generated stat/status/pattern/action mods can stack without adding collectible cards to the starting deck. The upgrade UI generates card -> element -> option choices from the current card definition, and costs scale by rarity plus per-card upgrade count.

notes.summary: Door opening animation normalizes each source frame onto a shared anchored canvas.
notes.details: door_opening.png is not a reliable equal-cell sheet. CombatBoardView slices the alpha-tight sprite bounds, places each frame on the max 256x383 transparent canvas anchored bottom-right, and scales the shared canvas from frame 0's used height against the static door used rect. Source-oriented doors anchor right/bottom; flipped side doors anchor left/bottom so the door footprint does not resize or drift while opening.

notes.summary: Labyrinth Crumble ships generated regular and header font faces; regenerate artifacts with tools/build_labyrinth_font.py.
notes.details: The generator emits Regular and Header TTF/TRES files plus the preview PNG. Regular remains the default theme font, while UiTypography routes card names, button text, title/room headers, and enemy intent titles through the Header face for a heavier stone display style. Do not hand-edit generated font binaries.

notes.summary: CombatBoardView board zoom fits rendered tiles through a cached layout.
notes.details: Board zoom still uses _tiles_in_draw_order() extents so hidden outer walls do not shrink the room, but those tiles/extents/tile width/origin must stay cached per state and Control.size. Calling _tiles_in_draw_order() or rebuilding extents from _tile_width()/_tile_center() hot draw paths caused severe animation and input lag.

notes.summary: Combat hand cards intentionally overlap, relying on CardWidget hover z-index.
notes.details: RunScene sets HandBox separation negative only in combat and computes hand card width with that overlap included, so cards can be wider without spreading across the full bottom bar. CardWidget's local hover/selected lift sets z_index=20, which keeps the active card visually in front of its overlapping neighbors.

notes.summary: Hand cards now fan through wrapper slots so hover lift stays local while the hand layout owns arch offsets and rotation.
Card art now uses a clipped keep-aspect-covered fill with larger default summary tokens that only step down when the rendered row count would exceed the details panel height.
Hand fan layout should reserve slightly less than the full arch height so edge cards can dip below the viewport, and slot z-order should stack left-to-right so the rightmost card stays uncovered.
Harrier and warden now use third-party idle sheets through the same-stem loader.
notes.details: assets/placeholders/units/harrier_idle.png and warden_idle.png are present again as 4x2 row-major 4080x2040 sheets with 1020px frames, so CombatBoardView auto-loads them from the harrier.png and warden.png art paths. The harrier sheet had 912 visible #ff00ff edge pixels; those were made transparent without otherwise altering the sheet.

notes.summary: Use typed helpers for GDScript Array[T] literals to avoid stricter Windows type checks.
notes.details: Godot on Windows rejected assigning a generic Array literal/conditional branch to Array[Vector2i] in blink shortcut previews. When a local, return value, or dictionary payload needs Array[Vector2i], build it with helpers such as _vector2i_array/_vector2i_values or an explicitly typed temporary before assignment.

notes.summary: Elemental combat rooms now seed 2-3 central-biased traps.
notes.details: Trap generation no longer scales max trap count down by depth. Combat and boss elemental rooms roll 2-3 traps, score candidates toward central traversal lanes, penalize edges/corner bands, avoid the player entry halo and occupied tiles, and keep modest spacing between traps.

notes.summary: Campfire bonfire art is rendered as presentation scene_props.
notes.details: RunScene passes scene_props=[{kind='campfire_bonfire', tile=Vector2i(4,4)}] for campfire mode. CombatBoardView loads assets/art/tiles/campfire_bonfire.png and scales it from tile width so the transparent sprite sits over the central 3x3 floor tiles without becoming terrain.

notes.summary: Combat hit polish stays presentation-driven through board effect metadata.
notes.details: RunScene now attaches preview damage projections and impact actor keys to the presentation/effect dictionary, while CombatBoardView renders projected HP loss, lethal tinting, reticles, path arrows, and hit flashes without changing CombatEngine rules. Future combat VFX should prefer adding board presentation metadata over mutating combat state just for visuals.

notes.summary: Lethal preview marker should stay a 64px dark fantasy pixel icon.
notes.details: assets/art/effects/lethal_skull.png replaced the large painterly skull with a 64x64 chroma-keyed pixel-art icon so lethal previews match assets/art/icons pixel density and dark fantasy style. CombatBoardView draws this icon over lethal targets instead of greying sprites or framing health bars.

notes.summary: Emaciated Man uses generated static PNG art.
notes.details: data/npcs.json now points emaciated_man art_path at res://assets/placeholders/units/emaciated_man.png. The asset is a 255x255 chroma-key-removed imagegen sprite with no idle sheet, so CombatBoardView should continue treating this NPC as static art unless a future emaciated_man_idle.png sheet is added.

notes.summary: Zekarion boss uses enemy footprints and summon-specific combat actions.
notes.details: The depth-4 lightning boss is represented as type zekarion with a 2x2 footprint. CombatEngine helpers expand enemy occupancy/targeting over footprint tiles, treat boss victory as killing Zekarion even if lightning_wisp minions remain, and use explicit lightning_strikes plus summon_minions action types for his special turns.

notes.summary: Debug boss fixtures are built by RunEngine, not RunScene
notes.details: The main-menu Zekarion shortcut should call RunEngine.create_debug_boss_run so it reuses room generation/combat creation and sets debug_boss_run=true. RunScene must treat that flag as non-persistent: save/quit, abandon, victory banking, and defeat loss should not mutate progression or saved-run slots; restart should rebuild the debug fixture instead of starting a normal run.

notes.summary: Zekarion idle animation uses the same-stem unit sheet loader
notes.details: assets/placeholders/units/zekarion_idle.png is a 4080x2040 4x2 row-major sheet copied from the user-provided download. data/enemies.json sets Zekarion idle_sheet_columns=4, idle_sheet_rows=2, row_major, ping_pong=true, idle_frame_seconds=0.1 so CombatBoardView loads it automatically from the zekarion.png art stem.

notes.summary: Lightning wisp idle animation uses a normal 16-frame same-stem loop
notes.details: assets/placeholders/units/lightning_wisp_idle.png is a 4080x4080 4x4 row-major sheet from the user download. data/enemies.json sets lightning_wisp idle_sheet_columns=4, idle_sheet_rows=4, row_major, idle_sheet_ping_pong=false, idle_frame_seconds=0.08 so CombatBoardView loads all 16 frames as a normal loop from the lightning_wisp.png art stem.

notes.summary: Lightning wisp idle cadence matches the downloaded GIF
notes.details: The user-provided A_diamond_shaped_emb... GIF has 16 frames with a 15-centisecond delay per frame. Keep lightning_wisp idle_frame_seconds at 0.15 with 4x4 row-major, ping_pong=false, so the same-stem PNG sheet plays at the preview GIF cadence rather than the faster 0.08s guess.

notes.summary: CombatBoardView unit shadows are broad silhouettes with stable idle anchors.
notes.details: Unit shadow projection is intentionally wider/deeper with minimal sideways shear so shadows read on top of tiles. Shadow foot anchoring uses the median opaque-bottom ratio across a unit type's idle frames, falling back to base/current texture bounds, so transient low-contact pixels such as crawler claw frames can animate the silhouette without moving the whole shadow.

notes.summary: Card rarity socket color lives in frame texture variants, not overlay controls.
notes.details: CardWidget selects assets/art/ui/card_frame_rarity_{starter,common,uncommon,rare}.png by rarity. Those PNGs are generated from card_frame.png by recoloring only the connected dark socket pixels, preserving the original metal/gold trim and exact slot geometry. Avoid returning to procedural PanelContainer/Control overlays for this marker; they leave gaps and cover the frame at card fan scales.

notes.summary: Campfire bonfire scene prop follows room type, not mode
notes.details: RunScene adds the campfire_bonfire scene_prop whenever the current room metadata type is campfire, even after leave_campfire changes mode back to room, so the bonfire remains visible until the player leaves the room. CombatBoardView loads assets/art/tiles/campfire_bonfire_idle.png as a 4x4 idle sheet for that scene prop.

notes.summary: Attack SFX assets should use WAV rather than MP3 in this project.
notes.details: Godot 4.6 headless tests reported no resource loader for the downloaded MP3 attack clips, while the same clips converted to WAV imported and loaded cleanly. Keep attack SFX under assets/audio/sfx as WAV unless the audio import pipeline is changed.

notes.summary: Treasure rooms use the fixed corner-pillar special-room layout.
notes.details: RoomGenerator now routes both campfire and treasure rooms through _apply_corner_pillar_layout so their interiors are ash floor except pillars at Vector2i(2,2), (6,2), (2,6), and (6,6). This keeps relic chest and bonfire center presentations clear instead of using random combat templates.

notes.summary: Relic rooms present their cache through a dedicated chest prop and bottom icon choices.
notes.details: Treasure rooms add a relic_chest scene prop at Vector2i(4,4) in RunScene presentation, drawn by CombatBoardView using assets/art/tiles/relic_chest.png with aspect-preserving scene-prop sizing. Relic choices are stage overlays in RunScene rather than bottom ChoiceBar buttons, and claimed relic HUD frames carry relic_id metadata for acquisition pulse animations.

notes.summary: Column torches use cleaned 4x4 idle sheets.
notes.details: column_torch_left/right remain the static fallback textures, but CombatBoardView now loads column_torch_left_idle.png and column_torch_right_idle.png as 4x4 overlays with COLUMN_TORCH_IDLE_FRAME_SECONDS=0.08. The sheets were cleaned for green/purple chroma speckles; the right sheet's non-flame torch body was partially normalized toward stable frame colors to reduce the frame-to-frame glow recolor while preserving flame flicker.

notes.summary: Idle redraw gating must track actual frame keys for mixed animation cadences.
notes.details: Using the fastest active idle interval as the only redraw tick caused slower column torches (7/60s) to be sampled on unit redraws (0.10s), repeating torch frames several times per loop. CombatBoardView now builds _active_idle_frame_key from unit, scene prop, and pillar torch frame indices so any visible animation frame change queues a redraw.

notes.summary: Card exhaust costs are virtual leading action rows.
notes.details: Card data still uses the legacy burn boolean for the exhaust-on-play cost to avoid save/progression/action-index churn. UI code should render it through ActionIconLibrary.cost_rows_for_card/rows_for_card as an Exhaust token; keep Burn icon/tooltip reserved for the fire status effect.

notes.summary: Card-play actions use a separate temporary turn bonus.
notes.details: The targetless card_play action increments card_play_bonus_this_turn and _card_play_capacity adds it alongside death_bonus_card_plays_this_turn. This keeps card-driven tempo distinct from enemy-death rewards while preserving cards_remaining_this_turn for UI, analytics, and tests; prepare_next_player_turn resets the action bonus.

notes.summary: Illusion cards use health/range actors
notes.details: The illusion card action stores health and range on the action, creates entries under combat_state.illusions with id/pos/hp/max_hp, and enemy targeting treats live illusions plus the player as actor targets. Animation steps carry target_losses/impact_actor_keys so non-player decoy damage renders correctly.

notes.summary: Illusion hover previews are presentation-only units
notes.details: RunScene emits presentation.preview_units with role illusion_preview only while a selected illusion action hovers a valid target tile. CombatBoardView draws those previews with translucent protagonist art, no HUD or shadow, and no procedural placement ring, keeping combat_state.illusions reserved for placed decoys.

notes.summary: Wood UI buttons use muted antique-gold raised 4.5:1 sprites
notes.details: button_wood_gold_*.png remain crisp 216x48 RGBA sprites, but the trim is muted toward the card_back/card_frame gold palette with sparse light glints instead of bright brass. UiSkin keeps BUTTON_TEXTURE_ASPECT at 4.5 and sizes small/standard/large/action buttons at 38/46/52/58 px; Pass/Skip/Cancel use the action height in the left bottom stack directly above the deck/discard piles, while reward +HP is rendered as a hand-row choice slot to the right of reward cards.

notes.summary: Headless playtest console exposes ambiguity-critical combat sources.
notes.details: Manual validation found that kill/card-play bonuses and block-only attacks were easy to misread, and target-choice indices could be confused with enemy indices. The harness now prints spent/remaining plays with kill/card bonuses, block/stoneskin removal, enemy intent payloads, pass previews, trap/path risks, skipped actions/logs/draws/restrictions, labels enemy targets, supports target eN, and logs card_played analytics after finish_player_card so play spend and health-cost effects match the console.

notes.summary: Pierce is an attack action flag that bypasses defenses.
notes.details: Cards express pierce as pierce: true on melee, ranged, aoe, push, or pull actions. Combat damage still uses final_damage_for_player_action and freeze multipliers, then bypasses block/stoneskin without removing them; ActionIconLibrary renders the damage number on a Pierce icon instead of adding a keyword token. Analytics logs pierce_actions and enemy_defense_bypassed for card_played payloads.

notes.summary: Card-facing Labyrinth art should be imagegen-derived, not procedural placeholder art.
notes.details: For new or replacement card art and action icons, inspect existing Labyrinth art/icon references, generate raster bitmap assets through the imagegen skill, resize to the exact project dimensions, and validate in CardWidget screenshots. Avoid SVG, PIL, canvas, or hand-coded placeholder visuals for final card assets unless the user explicitly asks for temporary placeholders.

notes.summary: Use fresh filenames for visual proof screenshots in Codex.
notes.details: Codex image previews may show cached content when a screenshot path is reused. For iterative visual QA, especially CardWidget renders, save each proof image with a unique timestamp or versioned filename and reference that new path in the response instead of overwriting the old screenshot.

notes.summary: Card art needs the existing transparent ragged window, not just 256x144 dimensions.
notes.details: New card art PNGs must have transparent corners and alpha statistics like existing assets; opaque black/full-bleed rectangles look wrong in CardWidget. Since CardWidget uses STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_COVERED in a wider art slot, inset generated focal content into the existing alpha window and verify with fresh-filename CardWidget screenshots.

notes.summary: CardWidget title nameplate width is calibrated to half card width.
notes.details: TITLE_NAMEPLATE_WIDTH_RATIO is 0.500 after visual calibration: this lets long-but-valid names such as Rallying Breath and Firebrand Volley render one point larger while the full card pool still measures at or below about 125 px on a 250 px card. Keep future title tuning systematic through the shared ratio rather than per-card overrides.

notes.summary: Air ambient wisps use full-body fade-and-drift wind motion instead of path reveal animation.
notes.details: Air rooms now pick directional wisp variants from frame 16 of ambient_air_wisp_frames.png/ambient_air_wisp_glow_frames.png and draw ambient_air_wisp_soft_particles.png as the soft body. The room seed chooses one left/right wind direction shared by all air wisps; alpha fades to zero over the movement cycle, and horizontal offset uses that shared direction so wisps drift like wind through the room rather than being drawn on/off. Fire remains on the separate quarter-size soft ember atlas.

notes.summary: Visual probes must redirect ProgressionStore paths before clearing saved runs.
notes.details: tests/ui_probe.gd and one-off screenshot probes should call ProgressionStore.set_storage_path/set_run_storage_path to probe-only user:// files before calling clear_saved_run or loading deterministic run states. Clearing without redirecting touches the player's real current_run.save and can wipe an active run. tests/run_tests.gd already uses test-only save paths.

notes.summary: Uncleared combat rooms defer exit reveal until victory
notes.details: Generated room metadata now defaults non-origin rooms to unrevealed; visibility should enter run_state only through explicit reveal calls. move_to_room does not reveal neighbors for uncleared combat/boss rooms, while finish_combat reveals them after marking the room cleared, so minimap and door exits stay hidden during active combat.

notes.summary: Combat action controls overlay wider targeting buttons without resizing the hand row.
notes.details: RunScene keeps ChoiceBar as a one-action layout placeholder during combat and parents the visible Pass/Skip/Cancel buttons to a root overlay positioned over that placeholder. This preserves the original pile/pass footprint while letting Skip+Cancel occupy nearby dead space without pushing the hand or top UI.

notes.summary: Run depth now uses sequence boss gates instead of ending at depth 4.
notes.details: RunEngine keeps four-depth sequences as the structure: local depths 1-3 are regular escalation and local depth 4 is a boss gate. The current playable cap is two active sequences (max depth 8) even though four are planned; depth-4 boss victories heal and reopen room mode, while only the final active boss or debug boss fixture enters victory.

notes.summary: Stun is removed as a gameplay status.
notes.details: Do not add new stun actions, badges, restrictions, analytics fields, or trap effects. Lightning Wisp Blinding Arc now uses shock, and Air traps are intentionally damage-only until a distinct Air secondary effect is chosen.

notes.summary: Relics use reusable effect hooks instead of per-relic id branches.
notes.details: Relic data defines reusable effects in data/relics.json. GameData applies card-action mutations from relics, while CombatEngine groups trigger hooks by timing, such as start-combat bonuses, status triggers, blink/long-move once-per-turn triggers, status-target damage, stoneskin thorns, death-status healing, and prevent-lethal effects. Add new effect types when needed, but do not branch on specific relic ids.

notes.summary: UiTooltipPanel factories should keep returning PanelContainer.
notes.details: tests/run_tests.gd types UiTooltipPanel.make_text as PanelContainer, so anti-clipping wrappers should be PanelContainer-based rather than returning MarginContainer or a generic Control.

notes.summary: Custom tooltip halos can come from Godot's TooltipPanel wrapper.
notes.details: Even when UiTooltipPanel's own StyleBoxFlat shadow is disabled, Godot may draw a default TooltipPanel style around custom tooltip controls. RunScene clears the scene theme's TooltipPanel/panel style with StyleBoxEmpty in _apply_tooltip_wrapper_style to remove that outer translucent halo.

notes.summary: Visual QA probes must redirect user:// storage before loading RunScene.
notes.details: Instantiating scenes/run_scene.tscn for screenshots can execute RunScene._ready(), which may start a new run, update progression.json, or clear user://current_run.save before test code injects a fixture state. Probe scripts should call ProgressionStore.set_storage_path and set_run_storage_path to unique probe/test files before adding RunScene to the tree, or otherwise avoid the live Godot app_userdata save slot.

notes.summary: Melee combat VFX uses a generated six-frame slash sheet.
notes.details: assets/art/effects/melee_slash_sheet.png is a 6x1 transparent imagegen spritesheet loaded by CombatBoardView through _load_sprite_sheet_frames. Keep melee attack polish in that raster sheet and frame playback rather than the old single melee_slash.png asset or procedural board indicators.

notes.summary: Card UI modifiers are token-level metadata.
notes.details: GameData records relic card-action changes under action._modifiers by field, while RunScene passes conditional combat bonuses such as Ember Lens through ActionIconLibrary token options like damage_modifiers. ActionIconLibrary merges both paths into token tone, modified markers, and per-token tooltips so future non-card modifiers should extend token metadata instead of adding card-level modifier tooltip paths.

notes.summary: Shortcut plans rank trap-free paths before shortest movement
notes.details: Headless target shortcuts should preserve the strategy guide's never-step-on-traps priority by preferring lower trap-risk movement paths before comparing movement distance/path length. This avoids playtest agents accidentally selecting an auto shortcut through a trap when a longer safe shortcut exists.

notes.summary: Hide combat board idle status text
notes.details: Do not render the combat board's top-left idle/hover status labels such as Pick Card, Drag Card, Pass, or hovered/selected card names. They overlap the elemental intensity HUD and the user considers them low-value; keep animation banners and non-combat labels separate.

notes.summary: Conditional card rows prefer compact light text
notes.details: Elemental intensity conditional blocks should keep 3-value-token rows slightly tighter than regular card rows, and render their values as light text with a dark outline for readability against the mostly opaque elemental background.

notes.summary: Conditional card rows size against visual width and active state
notes.details: Elemental intensity conditional rows should choose summary icon/label metrics against both available height and available visual width, including scaled card widgets such as discard pile previews. Requirement tokens can carry condition_active from RunScene; CardWidget uses it only for active glow styling, while inactive rows keep the same compact block layout.

notes.summary: Loop-closing rooms can gain dynamic outward escape links
notes.details: When a non-boss ring room has no revealed, unsealed same-depth-or-deeper exits after entry, combat victory, or loaded-run repair, RunEngine persists a loop_escape outward connection, reveals that destination, and stamps the door into current_room_layout. Static room_metadata still reports only the normal one-quarter outward links until run state needs the escape.

notes.summary: Fatigue damage visuals key off deck cycle deltas.
notes.details: RunScene detects fatigue for presentation by comparing before/after deck.cycles around CombatEngine.prepare_next_player_turn, then plays player impact, floating text, and the full-screen edge overlay. CombatEngine remains the source of fatigue damage rules; avoid adding visual-only state to combat dictionaries unless gameplay or analytics need it.

notes.summary: Movement animation state is staged at destination.
notes.details: RunScene stages moving actors at their destination before rendering movement frames, then uses CombatBoardView presentation unit_world_positions to interpolate the visible sprite and unit_draw_tiles for final layering. CombatBoardView exposes footprint-aware world_position_for_unit_origin and draw_tile_for_unit_origin so large enemies such as Zekarion animate from their visual footprint center and draw on the destination front tile instead of snapping to the anchor/origin if a presentation frame is missed.

notes.summary: Intensity-spending relics track gross gain and spend counters.
notes.details: CombatEngine increments elemental_intensity_gained_total whenever intensity is raised and elemental_intensity_spent_total whenever relic threshold rewards consume intensity. RunScene card_played analytics compares those counters so raise-and-consume relic payoffs do not disappear into a net before/after elemental_intensity delta.

notes.summary: RunScene root overlays need resize-driven relayouts.
notes.details: Root-level HUD overlays such as elemental intensity and combat choice buttons should not rely on a single immediate get_global_rect() from container placeholders after refresh. Relic/header reflow and ChoiceBar placeholder layout can settle a frame later, so connect resized signals and provide nearby fallback anchors like relic child bottoms or PilesBar to avoid stale gaps or top-screen jumps.

notes.summary: Battlefield trap blast VFX should use raster sprite assets without baked tile backgrounds or simple vector primitive overlays.
notes.details: Use transparent pixel-art decals rendered over the board's existing tiles; the user specifically rejected simple vector/line effects and generated tile/floor backgrounds for these blasts.

notes.summary: Foreground obstruction fading uses covered-sprite coverage threshold.
notes.details: Tall foreground props fade only when their overlap covers at least 25% of the behind entry rect, such as a unit, prop, loot item, trap, or terrain sprite. The threshold is intentionally based on the covered object's sprite rect rather than tile area so tiny edge slivers remain opaque.

notes.summary: Terrain health bars are contextual and preview-driven.
notes.details: CombatBoardView hides full-health idle terrain bars, shows them for damaged terrain or attack-highlighted terrain, and reads projected loss from damage_preview entries keyed as terrain_<id>. RunScene includes those terrain_<id> entries in player attack previews so terrain bars can render the same pending-loss overlay as unit health bars.

notes.summary: Headless playtest mirrors battlefield readability changes
notes.details: The manual harness board legend and combat state output intentionally list pickups, destructible terrain, and attackable adjacent-blast traps so text playtests preserve the same tactical information exposed in the board UI. Card resolution and analytics payloads also include terrain damage, terrain destruction, triggered traps, and collected pickups.

notes.summary: Keep normal game hover tooltips concise; put tactical instructions in playtest surfaces.
notes.details: The client board hover tooltip should show compact facts such as object name, HP, damage, and status effects. Extra guidance like terrain movement/LoS rules or trap trigger instructions belongs in tools/headless_playtest.gd and playtest docs instead of the normal game tooltip.

notes.summary: Campfires now choose between heal, carry, or level up.
notes.details: Campfire choice panels remain relic-style, but the third Draw strength from the flame option opens the level-up overlay when held embers meet ProgressionStore.next_level_cost. Linger heals 100 and continues; Embrace carries the current held ember count into the next run; Draw Strength spends held embers, assigns one stat point, exits campfire mode without healing, and continues the run.

notes.summary: Fixed-point scaling lives at data load boundaries.
notes.details: Cards and enemy definitions are scaled from old small data values through GameData before combat/UI use: HP, damage, block, heal, health cost, burn, poison, terrain and pickup amounts are 10x, while embers, draw/card-play counts, movement/range, freeze, shock, chain, and intensity remain unscaled. Progression stat bonuses are intentionally small displayed increments applied after this base scaling.

notes.summary: Relic descriptions are formatted display templates.
notes.details: data/relics.json descriptions may contain placeholders like {value}, {0.value}, {action.amount}, and {0.reward0.amount}. Player-facing relic copy should come from GameData.relic_def(), which replaces placeholders with effect-derived display values and applies fixed-point scaling for health, damage, block, stoneskin, burn, poison, and relevant reward/action amounts; GameData.relics() remains raw data.

notes.summary: Character levels now assign two distinct stat points.
notes.details: Progression level purchases use GameData.progression_stat_points_per_level from data/progression_levels.json, currently 2. Campfire Draw Strength requires choosing two different non-capped stats before confirm; ProgressionStore.purchase_level_with_stats validates the distinct stat list and allocates both points in the same purchase.

notes.summary: Lost embers are recovered through staged run recovery markers.
notes.details: RunEngine stages ProgressionStore recovery_marker data into the next run as room metadata at the death coordinate, forcing that room to a combat encounter and injecting dropped_embers loot into its combat layout. Combat collection increments combat_state.recovered_embers_total; RunEngine.set_combat_state applies only the new delta to held embers and clears the progression marker after reclaim.

notes.summary: Tile pickups, traps, and destructible terrain can occupy playable edge-band floor tiles.
notes.details: RoomGenerator no longer center-biases pickup/trap/terrain scoring or excludes playable corner floor tiles for destructible terrain. Terrain still avoids occupied tiles, the current entry halo, and placements that disconnect the remaining open floor.

notes.summary: Zekarion Tempest Breath is intentionally short-range.
notes.details: Tempest Breath uses move_toward 1 plus ranged range 3 because Zekarion's 2x2 gameplay footprint otherwise turns range 4+ into near room-wide coverage on open boss boards. Tests assert the opposite corner can remain outside the preview and actual hit.

notes.summary: Enemy threat previews assume player relocation and enemy-triggered hazards.
notes.details: enemy_threat_tiles uses a threat-only blocker set that erases the current player position while preserving terrain, traps, enemies, and illusions, so move/blink destinations account for routes through the old player tile. Attack previews also include blast tiles for traps an enemy can safely trigger from any reachable endpoint, keeping red zones conservative for enemy actions that can damage the moved player without the player changing blockers.

notes.summary: Elemental enemy reach budgets preserve movement safety.
notes.details: Air room enemies keep their +1 movement at medium/deep encounter depths, but elementalized attacks stay in a 3-4 range band so their max normal-roster move+attack reach is 8 instead of 9. Lightning room enemies keep high attack ranges, but positive move_toward/move_away actions lose 1 tile with a floor of 1 so their max normal-roster reach is 6.

notes.summary: Headless drag fallback attack uses fixed-point damage.
notes.details: Manual headless console mirrors real drag lanes: drag play uses printed text, drag attack uses the fixed-point fallback attack for 20 damage from base 2, and drag move remains range 2. Keep play-mode analytics comparisons aligned with those generated fallback action helpers instead of hardcoded raw arrays.

notes.summary: AOE orientation is chosen while aiming: hover centers the pattern, left/right or mouse-drag rotates it, and click stores orientation on the resolved action. Push/pull use force_direction, with only legal away/toward directions offered.
Immobilize is a boolean one-turn movement lock
notes.details: Cards express immobilize as immobilize: true, not a numeric stack. Combat stores it as a one-turn boolean unit condition consumed at the affected unit's next activation; enemies skip movement actions only, while player restriction blocks move and blink actions.

notes.summary: Avoid repeated side-profile ranged duel card art compositions
notes.details: For ranged card art, do not default to a hooded attacker on the left firing across a detailed scene at an enemy on the right. Vary compositions toward close-ups, over-the-shoulder views, environmental silhouettes, impact moments, or other card-specific framing unless that side-profile duel is explicitly requested.

notes.summary: Bone Dart is retired from active starter/reward pools
notes.details: Hamstring Shot replaces Bone Dart in GameData.starting_deck as the starter ranged card. Bone Dart remains defined with rarity starter so old saves, tests, or debug fixtures can still load it, but it is not marked starter and should not appear in starting_deck or reward_card_pool_by_rarity unless intentionally revived.

notes.summary: Turn order portraits should match the in-game unit sprites.
notes.details: For the initiative UI, portraits are sprite-derived thumbnails from assets/placeholders/units via tools/build_turn_order_assets.gd. Avoid generated reinterpretations that change character silhouette, tone, or style.

notes.summary: Turn-order UI animates from engine-provided order snapshots.
notes.details: Initiative turn-order changes should emit explicit turn_order steps from CombatEngine with before_order/after_order arrays. RunScene consumes those snapshots for pop/reslot animation instead of inferring from its possibly stale _combat_state during enemy animations, which prevents the player portrait from remaining active at the head after finish_player_activation.

notes.summary: Enemy guard intents must not materialize block before activation
notes.details: With initiative turns, revealed enemy intents are previews only. Block is cleared at the start of that enemy activation, applied by resolving the enemy block action, and persists until that same enemy's next activation starts. _apply_revealed_intent_blocks remains a no-op compatibility shim.

notes.summary: Turn-order previews show up to two activations per actor
notes.details: current_turn_order now includes the active/current slot plus projected follow-up slots for live actors. Queued enemies get a second projected activation at queued_time + base_initiative + current intent time, and the active player gets a projected next slot using base initiative plus time already spent plus any RunScene card-hover preview delta.

notes.summary: Turn-order animation removes only the active head entry
notes.details: Turn-order transitions must not infer removals from exact projected queue snapshots because projected times/seqs can change for multiple future entries. RunScene now uses active-head removal for the pop/fade, treats activation-only head changes as a style update, matches survivors by actor plus scheduled/projected role, and locks the panel width during reflow so the widget does not shrink or grow mid-animation.

notes.summary: Turn order header cap is 10 visible slots
notes.details: Four-enemy rooms show 10 turn entries including the player and fit acceptably; five-enemy rooms showing 12 were too wide, so cap the visible turn-order widget at 10 rather than 8.

notes.summary: Turn Clock portrait badges show relative ETA
notes.details: Turn order portrait numbers should display each entry's eta from the current initiative clock, not absolute scheduled time from combat start. Tooltips can still include the absolute Clock line as secondary context.

notes.summary: Card time costs use an overhanging animated clock badge
notes.details: The card time-cost badge is intentionally drawn as a larger procedural clock face that can overhang the card's top-right frame. CardWidget root clipping is disabled while art/title/detail controls keep their own clipping, and the clock hands animate while the card is hovered.

notes.summary: Clock badge animation uses real hand ratios
notes.details: The card time-cost badge hover animation advances one accelerated clock seconds value at 24 simulated seconds per real second. The second, minute, and hour hands are derived from that same value, so minute/hour movement stays proportional and the hands do not each run independent loops.

notes.summary: Procedural time clock uses layered bevel shading
notes.details: To keep the time-cost badge asset-free while matching raster card art better, draw it as layered brass/recess circles with directional highlight/shadow arcs, tick shadows, tapered polygon hands, a second-hand shadow, and a small dark number medallion. This avoids imagegen while making the badge feel less flat.

notes.summary: Time badge overhang should be symmetrical
notes.details: The card time-cost clock should keep only a small overhang past the frame, with matching top and right overhang. Avoid pushing it much farther right than upward; the balanced placement sits better on the card frame.

notes.summary: Card creation skill requires time costs
notes.details: The create-labyrinth-card skill now treats top-level card time as required card data, explains the 1-10 initiative-cost scale with 5 baseline, asks final reports to justify the chosen time, and notes that CardWidget renders the clock badge at runtime rather than through card art.

notes.summary: Depth-two fire rooms keep shallow burn pressure
notes.details: Early playtest runs repeatedly died to depth-two fire burn spirals before reaching the first boss. Fire enemy attacks now use a one-player-scale burn payload at encounter depths 1-2 and only restore the heavier burn payload at deeper standard rooms, while keeping the direct fire damage bump at depth 2.

notes.summary: Enemy target ties among player-side actors are randomized
notes.details: Enemy target selection gathers all closest valid player-side actor targets, including the player and live illusions, and uses combat RNG to choose among equal-distance ties. This applies movement, attack, push, and pull target selection, so illusions must be strictly closer only when reliable redirection is required.

notes.summary: Depth-two fire traps keep shallow burn pressure
notes.details: Fire traps now apply one-player-scale burn at depths 1-2 and reserve the heavier burn payload for deeper fire rooms, matching the combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp used after early playtest deaths from depth-two burn attrition.

notes.summary: Headless campfire choices mirror live continue options
notes.details: The manual playtest harness exposes campfire linger healing and level-up commands in addition to leave/rest. First-boss playtests should use campfires as continue-value rooms rather than forced run endpoints, reserving rest for banking and ending the run.

notes.summary: Headless console previews turn-order timing and combat keywords
notes.details: The manual playtest harness now mirrors the live turn-order widget more closely: combat state prints the current order plus pass-return timing, and each playable card row prints where the player's next turn lands after that card's time cost. Action text also surfaces pierce, immobilize, push, and pull keywords, with pierce defense-bypass included in target hints, card resolution notes, and analytics payloads.

notes.summary: Combat-only lateral routes gain an outward choice
notes.details: RunEngine's dynamic loop_escape now treats deeper exits, cleared rooms, free-value rooms such as treasure/campfire, and NPC rooms as preferred progress. If the only same-depth options are uncleared combat/boss rooms, the current room persists a revealed outward loop_escape so players can choose progression instead of being forced through lateral combat chains.

notes.summary: Headless console exposes deck pressure and partial action skips
notes.details: Combat hand output includes hand cap, draw/discard/burned counts, and next fatigue damage. Range-0 AOE action text lists affected tiles from the current state, and target-needing follow-up actions with no legal targets now pause with an explicit skip/cancel prompt instead of silently committing only earlier card effects.

notes.summary: Headless target labels include large enemy footprints
notes.details: Target labels in the manual harness now treat every tile in an enemy footprint as that enemy, so 2x2 bosses such as Zekarion are not shown as anonymous coordinates when targetable through a non-origin footprint tile.

notes.summary: Honest first-boss clear achieved after reverting pathing shortcut and retuning early combat.
notes.details: 2026-05-29 restarted playtest loop reverted the dynamic combat-only outward route shortcut. Balance changes made depth 1 easier, reward/build cards stronger, fatigue lower, crawler lunge blockable, and depth-3 generic scaling moderated. In honest r2, seed 5293102 cleared first boss after 7 pre-boss combats and 12 rooms including start; winning deck used Thunderline, Volt Surge, Static Lash, Hearth Rush, Hamstring Slice, Mirror Shard, and Updraft Bottle. Other r2 agents still mostly died to first depth-3 fire, so depth-3 fire remains the main wall despite goal success.

notes.summary: Text build-around card pack uses staged text_rule actions
notes.details: The design-only pack under output/buildaround_cards_100 keeps cards out of data/cards.json but uses proposed_cards_game_ready.json entries with a novel text_rule action plus presentation.mode=text_rule. Current CardWidget can only be coerced for previews with renderer-only overrides; selected build-around cards will need a real text-summary/card presentation mode so costs and rules text coexist before merging into the live pool.

notes.summary: Card FX coroutines must stop on mode changes
notes.details: Draw-card/card-proxy animations can continue after RunScene loads a non-combat state in probes or fast transitions. Guard FX loops with the current mode and layer liveness, and hide/drop top_level on proxy subtrees before queue_free so stale cards do not reappear over reward, campfire, or terminal overlays.

notes.summary: Hand fan measured width includes asymmetric right overflow
notes.details: The combat hand uses rotated rightmost cards with left-to-right z-order, so the visual edge can extend past the fan container's nominal card bounds even when card sizes fit. Keep an asymmetric right-overflow allowance in HandFanContainer's minimum/content width so CenterContainer shifts the fan slightly left and prevents edge cards from clipping at the viewport.

notes.summary: Motion probes should sample isolated animation helpers
notes.details: Calling RunScene._animate_enemy_phase_steps from a visual probe can overlap turn-order rebuild coroutines and produce freed Control casts that do not reflect normal gameplay. For motion screenshots, prefer deterministic direct helpers such as _animate_move_step with a duplicated combat state, then restore the board before sampling later effects.

notes.summary: Enemy damage floaters must clear the HUD stack.
notes.details: Enemy name/intent/HP labels occupy the tile center above units, especially near the lower board edge. Place enemy HP/block/stoneskin floaters in an above-HUD lane and keep renderer outlines enabled so impact feedback stays readable over floors and unit sprites.

notes.summary: Idle hand refreshes must clear stale CardFxLayer proxies once animations unlock.
notes.details: Top-level card FX controls can survive a draw/play animation and later appear as ghost hand cards during selection; keep cleanup gated by _animation_lock so active tweens are preserved but idle refreshes scrub leftovers.

notes.summary: UI probe output must clear nested artifact folders.
notes.details: tests/ui_probe.gd now recursively clears user://probes and owns fresh door_opening frame captures. Old nested folders such as door_opening or targeting can otherwise be copied into new visual-polish pass folders and make stale screenshots look authoritative.

notes.summary: Card combat numbers intentionally display fixed-point scale.
notes.details: Player-facing card action values use the universal 10x combat scale: Quick Stab should display 90 damage, not 9. Treat the trailing zero on fixed-point-scaled damage/heal/block/status values as intentional unless the design changes explicitly.

notes.summary: Large map modal backdrop should be fully opaque.
notes.details: A nearly opaque ColorRect scrim still allowed the high-contrast room header to ghost through above the large-map dialog margin in screenshots. Keep LargeMapScrim alpha at 1.0 unless the modal design changes to intentionally reveal the room behind it.

notes.summary: Hand fan bottom sink stays tiny to keep card frames readable.
notes.details: A 36px bottom overflow allowance let hovered/selected combat cards sit low enough for the viewport edge to clip their lower frame. Keep the default bottom overflow allowance around 6px and tests should guard that outer-card sink remains only slight while preserving the fan shape.

notes.summary: Level-up progression overlay uses a shorter dialog than the character sheet.
notes.details: The campfire Draw Strength overlay includes a confirm/cancel action row and opened low enough in 1920x1080 captures that the 660px character-sheet height clipped the action row. Keep the level_up progression dialog around 560px tall and let the stat list scroll so the action row remains visible.

notes.summary: Card-selection visual probes must reset player-turn state after pass-turn captures.
notes.details: The broad ui_probe sequence captures turn-order/pass-turn frames before Thunderline orientation frames. Without resetting RunScene card resolution plus combat_state current_actor/cards_played_this_turn/death_bonus_card_plays_this_turn/card_play_bonus_this_turn/player_turn_restrictions, _on_card_pressed can no-op and save stale non-selected screenshots even though the renderer works. Reset those fields before selected-card visual probes.

notes.summary: AOE motion probes should avoid lethal fixtures unless sampling death rewards.
notes.details: A Thunderline motion sample with low-HP targets killed an enemy, started death/ember reward coroutines, and later motion samples hit a freed mote. For isolated attack-effect frames, use high-HP targets or wait for the full reward sequence; keep lethal fixtures only for explicit death/reward visual QA.

notes.summary: Equipment compiles deck_cards from gear plus reward_cards
notes.details: Run state stores equipped_equipment, equipment_inventory, collected_equipment, and reward_cards. deck_cards is derived from equipped gear cards plus reward_cards and should be rebuilt through RunEngine after claims or equipment swaps. Equipment cards should set reward_pool:false so normal combat rewards remain elemental-only; equipment swaps are only allowed from room/campfire state.

notes.summary: Player equipment visuals render as board presentation overlays
notes.details: Equipped gear is passed from RunScene into CombatBoardView presentation.equipped_equipment and drawn as slot-anchored, rarity-ringed icon overlays on the player unit. This keeps gear visuals data-driven without regenerating or re-rigging the player idle sprite sheets; future sprite work should preserve the presentation payload or intentionally replace this overlay path.

notes.summary: Equipment gallery proofs should render through a sized SubViewport.
notes.details: OS window captures on macOS can cap the viewport height and silently clip lower equipment rows. The gallery proof script renders each slot into an offscreen SubViewport sized from the equipment count before saving, so all rows appear regardless of display height or high-DPI scaling.

notes.summary: Equipment cards should be unique and equipment-themed
notes.details: Equipment should not share granted card IDs across items. Each equipment card should read as something that specific item would enable mechanically and visually: swords grant sword attacks, shields grant blocks/bashes/guards, armor grants bracing/protection/repair, boots grant movement/footwork/trips, and trinkets grant small artifact effects. Avoid mechanically odd pairings such as adjacent melee attacks that pull targets, and keep equipment icons readable as tangible gear in the relic-like object style.

notes.summary: Resized card surfaces should scale native CardWidgets as one object
notes.details: For non-default card surfaces, RunScene wraps a native 250x352 CardWidget in a scaled parent instead of directly resizing the CardWidget. This keeps the frame border, rarity gem, art window, title, time badge, and action rows in the same proportions for hand cards, draw/discard piles, pile dialogs, equipment/card tooltips, upgrade previews, and drag/animation proxies. Direct CardWidget resizing can still distort nine-slice frame details.

notes.summary: Equipment drops use pity protection
notes.details: Equipment room drops remain seed/coordinate deterministic for normal rolls, but RunEngine tracks equipment_drop_misses and forces a weighted equipment drop after two eligible combat rooms without one. Loaded saves missing this counter migrate to the pity threshold so older in-progress runs are not stranded with no equipment after the feature lands.

notes.summary: Equipment tile loot uses icon-only pickup rendering
notes.details: User rejected the hand-drawn marker/plate/circle treatment for equipment pickups. Equipment loot should render as the actual equipment icon with the normal loot ground shadow and the same bottom-anchored tile footprint as potion and shield pickups; visibility should be solved by reliable drop placement/rates, not extra board shapes.

notes.summary: Equipment inventory tiles are single pointer targets
notes.details: Character-sheet inventory gear should treat the whole equipment tile as one hover/drag surface: child icon, labels, and layout controls are mouse_filter IGNORE, while the EquipmentInventoryTile parent owns tooltip and press/move/release drag. Gear drag uses EquipmentHeldProxy/EquipmentSwapProxy on EquipmentFxLayer instead of Godot native Control DnD so the held icon remains visible and avoids the forbidden OS cursor.

notes.summary: Magic rewards now use capped attunement
notes.details: Run state keeps reward_cards as collected reward-card history, while attuned_magic_cards is the six-slot active magic loadout that compiles into deck_cards alongside equipment. magic_inventory holds inactive reserve/default magic cards. Card rewards are claimed into reserve and require an out-of-combat character-sheet swap to become active.

notes.summary: Magic swaps live in a dedicated Magic tab
notes.details: The character sheet keeps Gear focused on equipment and a read-only current deck. Magic management lives in its own tab with six attuned spell slots, a learned/reserve spell panel, and the same read-only deck column; reserve/default magic tiles should not be created as drag targets on Gear.

notes.summary: Magic drag release can land on the destination tile
notes.details: Magic loadout swaps must let any MagicCardTile complete an active drag on left-button release, not only the tile that began the drag. Godot can deliver the release to the hovered destination spell tile, so target tiles need to call _release_magic_overlay_drag when _magic_overlay_drag_active is true.

notes.summary: Magic drops should resolve by visible held-card overlap
notes.details: For character-sheet Magic swaps, resolving only the cursor point is too strict because players position the translucent held spell over a slot/panel. The drop resolver should prefer exact tile hits, then held-card overlap, then the nearest opposite-side tile when the held card or cursor is inside the attuned/learned panel.

notes.summary: Async magic drag releases must be single-shot
notes.details: The Magic tab can receive the same mouse-up through both RunScene._input and MagicCardTile._gui_input while _release_magic_overlay_drag awaits the snap animation. Without a release-in-progress guard or marking input handled before awaits, the first release swaps the spells and the second release can swap them right back, appearing as a brief successful text change followed by a snapback.

notes.summary: Character menu badge fills should blend without visible bands
notes.details: Gear/Magic deck badges and magic tiles should avoid hard horizontal shadow cuts or obvious backing/underpaint seams. The backing uses per-strip gradients, the wash uses soft vertical and side shadow ramps, and the dim overscanned art fill stays low-opacity so it supports transparent art edges without reading as a separate layer.

notes.summary: Fresh Godot worktrees lack generated global-class cache
notes.details: New git worktrees do not have .godot/global_script_class_cache.cfg, so headless --script runs can report missing class_name types while exiting 0. Built-in tests/probes that must run in fresh worktrees should preload typed classes directly, and Godot wrappers should scan output for SCRIPT ERROR, Parse Error, Failed to load script, or TEST RESULT: FAIL instead of trusting exit code alone.

notes.summary: Parallel Godot wrappers use process-unique run namespaces
notes.details: tools/godot_task_runner.py and tools/visual_probe_runner.py generate default run/user-dir namespaces with nanosecond time plus process id, with the unique fragment early in the name so Godot custom_user_dir truncation cannot erase it. Same-task visual probes may run concurrently through the wrapper; avoid hand-picked identical --run-id values unless intentionally sharing state.

notes.summary: Autonomous implementation workers must be app-visible threads
notes.details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, implementation workers must run as user-visible Codex app threads with callable create_thread, read_thread, and send_message_to_thread equivalents exposed by the host session. If those tools are missing, stop before leasing/launching and report a blocker; do not silently fall back to hidden sub-agents, pre-created worktrees, terminal-only workers, or manual user-created threads without explicit same-turn user approval.

notes.summary: Orchestration requests authorize visible background threads
notes.details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, a request to use $orchestrate-labyrinth-tasks, run queued work, launch workers, start background tasks, or parallelize the queue is enough permission to create user-visible Codex app/background threads. Do not make the user separately say "create background threads" each time; still stop if the host session does not expose create/read/send app-thread tools.

notes.summary: Do not gate Labyrinth task orchestration on collisions
notes.details: User explicitly said to forget the collision concept for autonomous Labyrinth task orchestration and rely on normal git merge resolution. Keep queue schema fields valid if required, but do not block launching reviewed work because tasks may touch the same large files such as scripts/run_scene.gd.

notes.summary: Animation-locked hover callbacks must not refresh the board
notes.details: Enemy and player action animations can render an animated display_state that intentionally differs from _combat_state, with unit_world_positions/unit_draw_tiles carrying the in-flight sprite position. Hover signals from the board, hand, or rebuilt turn-order slots may still fire while _animation_lock is true; those callbacks may update hover bookkeeping but must not call _refresh_stage_view until the lock is released, or they can redraw stale _combat_state over the active animation and cause a visible rewind/snap.

notes.summary: Animation-locked board display must ignore resolved card previews
notes.details: Player card resolution can leave _preview_combat_state at the fully resolved position while _play_player_card sets _animation_lock and refreshes UI before _animate_player_card_resolution. During animation lock, _board_display_state should prefer authoritative _combat_state and let explicit _render_board_state calls provide in-flight frames; otherwise the player can flash at the destination, rewind, then animate there.

notes.summary: Initiative balance now uses intent-aware first enemy timing and live fast elemental rewards
notes.details: Initial enemy queue slots use enemy base initiative plus revealed intent time, with only an enemy-index stagger for readability; repeats use the same base+intent cycle. Player base initiative remains 9 with Agility floor 5. The June 2026 speed rebalance broadened card times so the starting deck averages about 3.56 time and normal elemental combat rewards span the full 1-10 range: Threaded Path is a time-1 Air movement/draw reward, Thorn Skewer is time 2, Firebrand Volley/Rime Shard/Spark Focus/Stone Plate are time 3, White Silence is time 9, and Wildfire Halo remains time 10. Practical pacing target: two fast cards return around initiative 13 and can lap slower enemies, two medium cards return around 18 without fast enemy double-ups, and two slow cards around 23 can let wisps/crawlers threaten doubles.

notes.summary: Campfire firelight should avoid banded halos
notes.details: For campfire room polish, do not render the bonfire glow as visible tile rings, hard circles, or an orange wash. Use blended soft light and visible ember motes that reuse the fire elemental room particle language so the effect reads organic and professional.

notes.summary: Campfire motes should taper upward from the fire bed
notes.details: For campfire ember motes, avoid an inverted-triangle plume where every spark starts at one center point and spreads outward. Prefer a slightly wider source across the bonfire sprite, with edge sparks fading sooner and central sparks rising a bit higher so the plume reads as a subtle right-side-up taper without becoming exaggerated.

notes.summary: Blink preview rift uses one textured smoke strip
notes.details: Blink preview suppresses generic path_tiles markers and draws assets/art/effects/blink_rift_preview.png as a single transformed rift mark, with vector ribbon only as a load-failure fallback. Preserve this direction for future polish so the preview does not expose circles, arcs, fray strokes, or other obvious construction primitives.

notes.summary: Generated traps are a high-value positional payoff
notes.details: Trap damage is intentionally tuned above weak direct ranged attacks: first-sequence standard depths deal 6/7/8 player-scale damage, first-sequence boss-depth traps deal 5 to avoid one-shotting full-health lightning wisps, and later sequences add 2 per completed sequence. Status payloads still use local encounter depth so early fire/poison traps keep shallow pressure.

notes.summary: Campfire bonfire alpha cleanup is baked into PNG assets
notes.details: CombatBoardView draws assets/art/tiles/campfire_bonfire.png and campfire_bonfire_idle.png directly; no runtime alpha cleanup is applied to the campfire prop, and no unaltered animation source is checked in. Future repairs should use frame-local exterior flood-fill to preserve border-connected transparency while filling only enclosed low-alpha islands inside the flame/smoke artwork.
